content.text:
`out/module.ts` is written and type-checks with no errors. The only `tsc` errors are in the original `src/module.ts`, because lodash isn't installed. I could not run the original code, so I did not compare outputs against it. `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 553 bytes (min+gzip) and 110 bytes of own code. I could not get a baseline for the original's own-code size either, since lodash isn't installed.

| Function | Before (lodash) | After (es-toolkit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applyPatch` | `merge` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` |
| `toTitle` | `startCase` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit` |
| `toLookup` | `fromPairs` | `zipObject` from `es-toolkit`, with a one-line adapter |

- **`merge`:** I read the source, and the strict version merges arrays by index and plain objects recursively, as lodash does. `null` and scalar patch values overwrite the base value, as in lodash. I didn't compare the two directly.
- **`startCase`:** I ran a few inputs through it, such as `"Size UserUsersize."` → `"Size User Usersize"` and `"a1b"` → `"A 1 B"`. The results match what I remember lodash returning, but I couldn't check them against lodash.
- **`fromPairs`:** There is no strict version; it exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`. I used `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))` instead. Later pairs override earlier ones, so the result is the same for duplicate names, which can occur in the input range.

The compat `fromPairs` variant bundled to 607 bytes with 82 bytes of own code. I chose `zipObject` because the bundle is 54 bytes smaller, at the cost of about 28 more bytes of my own code. If the own-code allowance is tight, the compat version is the one to swap in.

No lodash import remains, and nothing was installed.
